name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-5
description: 5" 720x1280 MIPI-DSI panel (HX8394) with GT911 touch on an ESP32-P4, an ES8311 speaker codec, a TF card and Wi-Fi through its ESP32-C6. Compiled, not yet seen on a board.
verify: Nobody at LCD Wizard has had this board: the export for it compiles and has not been seen on the panel. A user had one running from an LCD Wizard export he changed by hand to Waveshare's own settings and Waveshare's copy of GFX Library for Arduino; this preset carries those settings, read again from Waveshare's Arduino examples for the board, on the library as it is published: the HX8394 under Waveshare's register table, two lanes at 700 Mbps, 58 MHz, hsync 20/20/40, vsync 4/10/24, the panel's reset on GPIO 27 - active high, so the generated code pulses it itself, where the library's own pulse would leave this panel in reset - and the backlight on GPIO 26, lit when high and dimmed by PWM (Waveshare say a steady level does not light it, and the export's PWM never holds it steady). A design on this preset starts on revision 3 of the ESP32-P4, which Waveshare's own Arduino examples for the board build for; for a chip before revision 3 (the upload says "revision v1.x"), choose that under Hardware > Board > Chip revision. The GT911 has no reset or interrupt line driven and may answer at 0x14 instead of 0x5D. The TF card (SDMMC, 4-bit) and the ES8311 speaker codec (amplifier on GPIO 53) are in the kit. Wi-Fi is the ESP32-C6 beside the P4, in the kit as the Wi-Fi co-processor on the ESP32 core's own SDIO lines (CLK 18, CMD 19, D0-D3 14-17, reset 54) - Waveshare publish no pins for it, and their own Arduino Wi-Fi example uses those defaults; it has to run ESP-Hosted of the core's release, which the board prints at start (see the README). Wi-Fi through it compiles and has not been on a board. Not driven: the two ES7210 microphones, the camera connector and the C6's Bluetooth; ESP-NOW does not go through the C6.
